title: Existing conventions, portable guidance and proportionate planning
summary: Apply source precedents and review conformity. Keep bootstrap/tool coverage portable and prevent duplicate capability ownership.
description:
Purpose: Apply source precedents and review conformity. Keep bootstrap/tool coverage portable and prevent duplicate capability ownership.

Current state: this phase is planned; current production persistence remains JSON until the SQLite/API migration is implemented. Reuse existing capabilities instead of creating another planner.

Deliverables and sole owners:
- P119(F025)/T467: Source-backed use of existing conventions before implementation and review of the resulting diff.
- P119(F025)/T468: Portable installed bootstrap and API-delivered operating guidance for every supported harness.
- P119(F025)/T469: Proportionate planning that discovers existing capability ownership before creating work.

Execution contract:
Follow the task dependencies and the phase priority in the rebuilt F025 plan. Keep coherent phase work and recover approved detours; do not introduce a global task queue or silently preempt active work. Use the user-scoped service/SQLite boundary, explicit workspace identity, complete bounded context and revision-bound evidence wherever applicable.

Acceptance:
Each task proves its stated outcome; preserve IDs/history, single-owner decisions and phase handoffs. Mechanical parent/dependency effects are consistent; semantic review is factual, reviewed-unchanged or explicitly pending. Native/provider/installed claims need their actual owner evidence.

This is one current phase contract, replacing the accumulated historical amendments. Do not migrate user data or perform Git/release actions merely because the plan is registered.

Child-contract reconciliation: Generic bootstrap retrieves current project guidance through APIs. Source precedent analysis and final conformity evidence remain required even when instructions have been delivered.

tasks.title: Add evidence-backed source analysis and conformity review to existing workflow
tasks.description:
Outcome: Source-backed use of existing conventions before implementation and review of the resulting diff.

Current implementation: Project Guidelines and source-analysis instructions already exist; agents ignoring them is an enforcement/visibility problem, not missing generic advice.

Implementation responsibility:
- Use existing task analysis fields/notes to record applicable guidelines, closest implementation precedents, conventions, reuse and intended integration before code edits.
- Support text/source inspection before semantic providers exist; record genuine absence of precedents and resolve material rule gaps through discussion.
- Review the actual diff against chosen precedents and explicit rules, recording concrete conformity evidence and limitations.
- Invalidate analysis after relevant source/context changes. Preserve the warning-only no-task guard and truthful harness interception coverage; do not add an unapproved source-write denial policy.

Acceptance and evidence:
- A cold worker can find the relevant conventions and real examples for a component/module.
- Reading/ticking/tests alone cannot certify architectural conformity.
- Review provenance is tied to source/configuration and becomes stale when the implementation changes.

tasks.title: Synchronize the operating protocol across harnesses and context-loss events
tasks.description:
Outcome: Portable installed bootstrap and API-delivered operating guidance for every supported harness.

Current implementation: Canonical core/plugin skills already exist, but MCP/Pi point at .planner/SKILL.md and custom docs rely on local files that disappear after migration.

Implementation responsibility:
- Extend the canonical guide and generated plugin sync pipeline, preserving useful skill/rule/hook patterns without a Claude-only authority.
- Provide installed bootstrap discovery for MCP harnesses and Pi; load the descriptor/service and deliver canonical/project guidance as actual content from APIs.
- Preserve imported customized skills and document links in logical DB folders. A skill stored in DB is not automatically a native discoverable harness skill.
- Inventory tool/command coverage and update all local-file pointers, prompts and lifecycle wording; do not expose database paths or require direct DB access.
- Exercise new session, compaction, changed Guidelines and harness switch, with explicit restoration/limits where native hooks are absent.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Existing planner operations remain available on supported MCP/Pi integrations after migration.
- A new agent with installed bootstrap can load the project without .planner/SKILL.md.
- Custom guidance is preserved and delivered; generated copies express one consistent protocol.

tasks.title: Prevent duplicate capability ownership and unnecessary task creation
tasks.description:
Outcome: Proportionate planning that discovers existing capability ownership before creating work.

Current implementation: Granular planner CRUD and checklists exist. Repeated task creation can outpace completion and leave parent scope/dependencies contradictory.

Implementation responsibility:
- Expose compact related-task/phase ownership discovery using structured filters and search before add/split proposals.
- Distinguish a new independent deliverable from implementation steps, evidence updates or an adaptation to an existing owner.
- Prefer checklist additions for steps; preserve task identity when moving or updating. Give a reason when a new outcome genuinely needs a task.
- Apply T496 parent/dependency postconditions on creation/move and show unresolved scope obligations rather than copying child prose upward.

Acceptance and evidence:
- The same capability is not silently registered twice under different phases.
- Large work can keep one task and an attributable changeset without listing every modified function.
- Discovery and reconciliation use bounded relevant results, not unconditional full-plan reads.
